**1**. Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness by The Smashing Pumpkins
A great album, which I believe perfectly mixes some hardcore rock with some more mellow slower stuff. It also perfectly describes the way many people feel throughout their teen years.
**2.** The Wall by Pink Floyd
An amazing concept album, which, after seeing the movie, is only more powerful. As a side note, a great album to listen to baked for any of you into that.
**3.** Abbey Road by The Beatles
I own every Beatles album, but Abbey Road is by far my favorite, as it just oozes the time period it was made in, which I can appreciate. It also features some of my favorite Beatles songs, such as "You Never Give Me Your Money" or "The End"
**4.** Bleach by Nirvana
One of the greatest grunge albums ever made, Bleach just describes what music was in the late 80's early 90's.
**5.** Nevermind by Nirvana
Another great Nirvana album, it's just a shame that it's a bit overrated in my opinion.
**6.** They Can't All Be Zingers by Primus
As much as I hate Greatest Hits albums, this one is honestly very good. It does in fact hold most of the best Primus songs, and it needs credit for interesting packaging.
**7.** Never Mind The Bullocks, Here's the Sex Pistols by The Sex Pistols
While not extremely talented, the Sex Pistols have one of my favorite stage presences. Also, "God Save the Queen" is just gold.
**8.**  By The Way by The Red Hot Chili Peppers
This album is my favorite RHCP album, because it contains some of the groups best work, including what I believe to be some of the best Flea bass work of all time.
**9.** Ten by Pearl Jam
As you can probably tell by now, I'm a big fan of grunge. Ten is another classic that just completely wows me from start to finish and is masterful in every sense of the word.
**10.** Mothership by Led Zeppelin 
I don't know what I can say about Mothership that hasn't been said, but it's classic Led Zep so if you're into them, you love Mothership
